title: Multi-Article Line Formatter
prompt:
Implement `format_articles(articles, width) -> list[str]`. Each article is a string. Normalize whitespace by splitting into tokens and placing one space between adjacent tokens. Return border-free output lines in the original token order. Insert exactly one `"----"` separator between every adjacent pair of input articles, never after the final article. An empty article emits no text lines but still participates in those separators. Separators are structural and are exempt from the line-width limit.

For the punctuation characters `.,;:!?`, a token beginning with one of them must stay with its preceding word or token group, separated by one space. Consecutive punctuation-leading tokens belong to that same indivisible group. A punctuation-leading token at the start of an article has no predecessor and is invalid. Do not split words or groups.

Greedily pack the indivisible groups into lines of at most `width` characters. If a group does not fit after the current line, move the whole group to the next line. If any word or group is longer than `width`, reject the input with `ValueError` or `AssertionError`; never produce an overflowing text line. Do not rebalance lines to avoid a final one-word line.

`width` must be positive; reject an invalid width with `ValueError` or `AssertionError`. Return `[]` for an empty `articles` list with a valid width.

example.reasoning: The punctuation token and its preceding word move together so every text line stays within the width.
